question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool execution mode to agent-core, and should that depend on new tool concurrency-safety metadata before early execution is allowed?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix changes core runtime semantics and safety policy rather than repairing a narrowly broken existing contract.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for execute-on-parse scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

options.title: Wait For Tool Safety Metadata
options.body: Treat early execution as blocked until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962 or an equivalent concurrency-safety contract exists.

options.title: Defer Runtime Semantics Change
options.body: Leave current post-stream parallel batching as the only supported core behavior if maintainers decide early execution is too risky for now.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for execute-on-parse scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: His recent commits most directly touch agent-core extraction and truncated tool-call handling across the central surfaces involved.
